_doc: Point-in-time fact sheet for SO retrospectives (retro/build_so.py). Every value is tied to a source and becomes visible only on or after that source's 'published' date: a filing accepted after the 16:00 ET close is dated the next trading day ('filed' keeps the acceptance time, US Eastern; EDGAR records no time before 2003). Southern Company's earnings 8-Ks of Q2 2007 to Q3 2009 were accepted before the open or during the session on the release day, each a Wednesday or Thursday, and the 10-Ks weeks after the Q4 releases, so a Q4 print carries its year's actuals (fy_actual) until the 10-K. No filing guides EPS, revenue or a margin in numbers (the releases say earnings guidance is discussed on the analyst call; no transcript or slides are filed). Generated by a script from row strings of the filings (each checked with retro/tools/verbatim.py); every growth rate, margin, margin change and rule-T value is computed. See retro/README.md, 'SO'.

distributions.note: the spin-off of Mirant: 'On April 2, 2001, the tax-free distribution of Mirant shares was completed at a ratio of approximately 0.4 for every share of SOUTHERN common stock held at record date.' (SO4); Yahoo books it as a 10000:6109 split on 2001-04-03, the first day the stock traded without it; it is not a split, so its factor is undone for the days before and prices stay as traded (the MAR, PFE and BMY 'distributions' rule). The P/E windows of 2008-2009 start in 1998-1999, so the days to 2001-04-02 carry Mirant's value against EPS from continuing operations, which excludes it (the MAR judgement call)

margin.sources: operating margin (operating income on total operating revenues), each change from the latest 10-K by FY2006 whose statement of income tabulates both years; 1998 from the FY1999 10-K, which still consolidated Southern Energy (later Mirant); the FY1998 10-K's operating income is after income taxes, a different measure, so 1997 has no value (the AVGO rule)

price_basis: NYSE common stock as traded: Yahoo's 2-for-1 split of 1994 precedes every per-share fact; its 10000:6109 'split' of 2001-04-03 is the Mirant distribution, undone ('distributions')
